Label one of the large, round, thick-walled empty cells in the lower right cluster as a xylem vessel.
Each label needs a line that ends on the correct tissue (xylem inside, phloem outside it, sclerenchyma outermost).

questions.question: How many of three statements about phloem are correct? (1) connected to other cells by plasmodesmata, (2) transports water and organic solutes, (3) translocation moves substances in phloem. A none, B one, C two, D three.
questions.answer: C two (statements 1 and 3 are correct)
steps: Statement 1 is correct: sieve tube elements connect to companion cells through plasmodesmata.
Statement 2 is wrong: phloem transports organic solutes, while water is transported by xylem.
Statement 3 is correct: translocation is the movement of substances in the phloem.
Two correct statements give answer C.

questions.question: Name a structural molecule in the cell wall of plant cells and in the cell wall of prokaryotic cells.
questions.answer: Plant cell wall: cellulose. Prokaryotic cell wall: peptidoglycan (murein).
steps: Plant cell walls are built mainly from cellulose microfibrils.
Bacterial cell walls are built from peptidoglycan (murein), a polymer of sugars and amino acids.
Both give the cell rigidity and shape.

questions.question: Explain how the arrangement of molecules contributes to the physical properties of the cell walls of sclerenchyma fibres.
questions.answer: Cellulose chains are arranged in microfibrils held by hydrogen bonds, giving tensile strength; lignin deposited in layers adds rigidity and resistance to compression.
steps: Cellulose molecules are long unbranched chains of beta-glucose.
Parallel chains are cross-linked by hydrogen bonds to form microfibrils, which resist stretching.
Microfibrils are arranged in layers, which resist forces from several directions.
Lignin is deposited between and around the microfibrils, making the wall rigid and compression-resistant.

questions.question: Which tissue is involved in the transport of magnesium ions in a plant? A amyloplast, B plasmodesmata, C sclerenchyma, D xylem.
questions.answer: D xylem
steps: Mineral ions such as magnesium are absorbed by roots and carried upwards in the xylem.
Amyloplasts and plasmodesmata are cell structures, not tissues.
Sclerenchyma gives support and does not transport ions, so D is correct.

questions.question: Explain how a lack of magnesium ions could result in yellow leaves and reduced growth of the vine plant.
questions.answer: Magnesium is needed to make chlorophyll; less chlorophyll means leaves are yellow and less light is absorbed, so less photosynthesis and less glucose for growth.
steps: Magnesium ions are a component of chlorophyll.
Without magnesium, less chlorophyll is made, so leaves appear yellow.
Less chlorophyll means less light is absorbed, so photosynthesis slows down.
Less glucose is made, so less energy and fewer materials are available for growth.

questions.question: Discuss the benefits of adding crushed eggshells to the soil around vine plants, using the graphs of leaf area, shoot length and chlorophyll content.
questions.answer: Adding crushed eggshells (a source of calcium ions) increased leaf area, shoot length and chlorophyll content, with the largest effects after about 3 to 4 weeks.
steps: Leaf area: with eggshells it reaches about 2800 cm^2 at 52 days compared with about 1200 cm^2 without (more than twice, +133%), and the error bars separate from day 31 onwards, so the difference is probably significant.
Shoot length: by day 52 plants with eggshells are about 202 cm long against about 80 cm without (+150%); the lines are about the same until day 24 and then diverge.
Chlorophyll content: higher with eggshells at all times after day 10, about 37 a.u. against 29 a.u. at day 52 (+26%), so the leaves can absorb more light for photosynthesis.

Explanation: calcium ions form calcium pectate in the middle lamella and help cell wall formation, so cell growth and division are better; a larger leaf area and more chlorophyll mean more photosynthesis and more growth, which could give more fruit.
Eggshells are also a waste product, which is cheap and sustainable, and the calcium carbonate may reduce soil acidity.
Limitations: there is no benefit in the first 3 weeks; the study was on one type of vine for 52 days and fruit yield was not measured.

questions.question: Suggest how the mean increase in dry mass of a pumpkin could be estimated in Step 1 of the investigation.
questions.answer: Dry a sample of pumpkins at the start and another sample of the same age after 792 hours in an oven until their mass is constant, then subtract the mean dry mass.
steps: A pumpkin cannot be dried and then grown on, so use a large sample of similar pumpkins: collect some at the start and another group after 792 hours of growth.
Cut up each pumpkin and dry it in an oven at a fixed temperature (about 80 degrees C), weighing it repeatedly until the mass is constant, so all water has gone.
Calculate the mean dry mass of each group; the mean increase in dry mass = mean at 792 h minus mean at the start.

questions.question: Explain why Crafts and Lorenz used dry mass in this investigation.
questions.answer: Dry mass excludes the variable water content of the fruit, so it measures only the organic material (sucrose and other solutes) that has been translocated.
steps: Fresh mass of plant tissue varies greatly with water content.
Drying removes water, so the dry mass reflects only dry organic material.
This means the increase in dry mass reflects the amount of organic solutes translocated into the fruit.

questions.question: Which letter (P, Q, R or S) on the light micrograph of a stalk cross-section points to the phloem?
questions.answer: C: R
steps: Phloem has small thin-walled cells containing sieve tubes and companion cells and lies on the outer side of the large xylem vessels in the vascular bundle.
P points to a large, empty thick-walled xylem vessel, and Q points to a large parenchyma cell outside the bundle.
R points to the dense area of small cells at the outer edge of the bundle, which is the phloem; S points to the supporting tissue beside the vessels.

questions.question: Describe a method that could be used to determine the cross-sectional area of the phloem in Step 2.
questions.answer: Measure the diameter of the sieve tubes in the micrograph using an eyepiece graticule or scale bar, convert to actual size, then calculate the area as pi x r^2 and sum the tubes.
steps: Calibrate the eyepiece graticule against a stage micrometer, or use the scale bar on the micrograph.
Measure the diameter of several sieve tubes in the phloem region.
Convert the measurements to actual size using the magnification.
Calculate the cross-sectional area of each tube using pi x r^2 and add them to give the total phloem sieve tube area.

questions.question: Give a reason why only the cross-sectional area of the sieve tubes, rather than the whole phloem tissue, was estimated.
questions.answer: Translocation of organic solutes occurs only through the sieve tubes, so only their area is relevant to the rate of flow.
steps: Translocation (movement of sugars) occurs through sieve tubes.
Other phloem tissues such as companion cells, parenchyma and fibres do not carry the sap flow.
So only the sieve tube area is needed to calculate the rate of translocation.

questions.question: What are the units for the rate of translocation calculated in Step 4? A g cm-2 hr-1, B g cm2 hr-1, C g cm-3 hr-1, D g cm3 hr-1.
questions.answer: A g cm-2 hr-1
steps: Rate of translocation = mass transported / (cross-sectional area x time).
Mass is in g, area in cm2 (giving cm-2 in the denominator), and time in hours (hr-1).
So the units are g cm-2 hr-1, answer A.

questions.question: Which structures enable E. coli to stick to the surface of fish? A capsule and flagellum, B capsule and pili, C flagellum and pili, D flagellum and ribosomes.
questions.answer: B capsule and pili
steps: Pili are hair-like projections that help bacteria attach to surfaces.
The capsule is a sticky outer layer that helps bacteria adhere to surfaces.
Flagella are for movement, not sticking, and ribosomes are for protein synthesis.

questions.question: Explain what is meant by sustainable in the context of plant-based packaging compared with oil-based packaging.
questions.answer: Sustainable means meeting present needs without reducing the ability of future generations to meet theirs, so plant-based packaging uses renewable resources and biodegrades.
steps: Sustainable means meeting current needs without using up resources needed in the future.
Plant-based packaging is made from renewable plant material that can be regrown.
Oil-based packaging uses a finite resource and does not biodegrade, so it is not sustainable.

questions.question: Comment on the results of the investigation into packaging material and the number of S. aureus colonies on fish, using the table of means and standard deviations.
questions.answer: Pine wood packaging gave by far the biggest decrease in S. aureus (7.14 colonies cm^-2); poplar wood had a small effect and HDPE and polystyrene had almost none.
steps: Pine wood reduced S. aureus by 7.14 +/- 0.28 colonies cm^-2, about 9 times the decrease with poplar wood (0.79) and about 90 times that with polystyrene (0.08).
HDPE had no effect (0.00 +/- 0.02) and polystyrene almost none (0.08 +/- 0.02), so oil-based plastic packaging does not kill the bacteria.
The pine SD is small and its range (6.86 to 7.42) does not overlap with the others, so the difference is significant; poplar has a large SD (0.44), so its effect is less certain.

Wood is more antibacterial than plastic, probably because it contains antimicrobial chemicals such as resins, so plant-based (pine) packaging is better for keeping fish safe and is also more sustainable.

questions.question: Suggest one advantage to this skin bacterium of having a capsule.
questions.answer: The capsule protects the bacterium from phagocytosis by white blood cells and from drying out.
steps: A capsule is a thick outer layer of polysaccharide.
It makes the bacterium harder for white blood cells to engulf (phagocytosis).
It also helps the bacterium resist drying on the skin.

questions.question: Suggest why this type of bacterium does not need a flagellum.
questions.answer: It does not need to move far, because it enters through a cut and spreads by growth and division on the skin surface, so a flagellum (for swimming) is not needed.
steps: A flagellum is used for movement of the bacterium.
This bacterium lives on the skin surface and enters through a cut, so it does not need to swim long distances.
It spreads passively and by division, so it can do without a flagellum.

questions.question: Which structures would be found in a bacterial cell? 1 cell membrane, 2 cell wall, 3 ribosomes. A 1 and 2 only, B 1 and 3 only, C 2 and 3 only, D 1, 2 and 3.
questions.answer: D 1, 2 and 3
steps: All bacterial cells have a cell surface membrane (1).
Bacteria have a cell wall made of peptidoglycan (2).
Bacteria have 70S ribosomes for protein synthesis (3).
So all three are present: answer D.

questions.question: Calculate the standard deviation of the inhibition zone diameters for flucloxacillin, using the student's table and formula, in mm.
steps: Fill in the table: for 7.5, x - mean = 7.5 - 9.0 = -1.5 and (x - mean)^2 = 2.25.
s = square root of (6.5 / (n - 1)) = square root of (6.5 / 2) = square root of 3.25 = 1.80 mm.

questions.question: Which explains why the student would want to calculate standard deviation(s) in this experiment? A to see how widely the diameter values differ from the mean diameter, B to see if observed results differ from expected results, C to see if there is a correlation, D to see the most frequent number.
questions.answer: A to see how widely the diameter values differ from the mean diameter
steps: Standard deviation measures the spread of data around the mean.
It shows how much variation there is in the diameter values.
B describes comparing observed with expected data (a statistical test), C is about correlation and D describes the mode, so A is correct.

questions.question: Which percentage of the initial group of 2444 patients were placed in group B? A 8.3%, B 8.5%, C 49.5%, D 50.5%.
steps: Group B contained 203 patients out of the initial group of 2444 patients.

questions.question: Suggest how this study could be carried out as a double-blind trial.
questions.answer: Neither the patients nor the clinicians know which treatment each patient receives, for example by giving identical-looking treatments labelled with codes held by someone not involved in the assessment.
steps: Patients are randomly allocated to the flucloxacillin alone group or the flucloxacillin with clindamycin group.
The two treatments are made to look identical, e.g. by using a placebo or coded packaging.
The codes are kept by an independent person until the results are analysed.
Neither patients nor the staff measuring the leg circumference know which group they are in, which avoids bias.

questions.question: Comment on the results of the trial comparing the mean difference in leg circumference at 5 and 10 days after treatment with flucloxacillin alone and with clindamycin added.
questions.answer: The swelling difference fell between 5 and 10 days in both groups, and group B (smaller swelling at both times) improved more; if B received the added clindamycin, the combination appears better, but only slightly and without statistics.
steps: Both groups improved: the mean difference in circumference fell from 2.18 to 1.77 cm in group A (a fall of 19%) and from 2.04 to 1.42 cm in group B (a fall of 30%).
Group B had less swelling than group A at both times: 0.14 cm less after 5 days (6% less) and 0.35 cm less after 10 days (20% less).

The difference between groups is therefore greater at 10 days, so the added drug (taking group B as the flucloxacillin plus clindamycin group) appears to speed up the reduction of swelling, although the page does not state which group had which treatment.

Limitations: no standard deviations or significance test are given so we cannot tell if the difference is real, the difference at 5 days is very small, and the patients were all male, so the result may not apply to females.

questions.question: Name the structure labelled X in the diagram of guard cells from wheat plants.
questions.answer: Vacuole
steps: X points to the large clear elongated sac inside the guard cell (the pale area without chloroplasts), which is the vacuole.
Under water stress the vacuole loses water, and the guard cell becomes flaccid so the pore closes.

questions.question: Suggest why closing the pores reduces water stress in the plant.
questions.answer: Closing the stomata reduces transpiration, so less water vapour is lost from the leaves.
steps: Stomata are pores in the leaf through which water vapour diffuses out.
Closing them restricts the diffusion of water vapour out of the leaf.
Less water is lost by transpiration, so the plant suffers less water stress.

questions.question: Which is the percentage change in chlorophyll content when wheat has water stress? A +46.9%, B -46.9%, C -88.2%, D +88.2%.
steps: Chlorophyll content without water stress is 3.2 mg dm^-3 and with water stress is 1.7 mg dm^-3.
Percentage change = -1.5 / 3.2 x 100 = -46.9% (a decrease), so B.

questions.question: Deduce how water stress could affect the growth of wheat plants, using the three graphs and your own knowledge.
questions.answer: Water stress greatly reduces growth: it cuts survival from 100% to about 20%, cellulose content from about 25% to about 20%, root length from about 8.9 cm to about 4 cm and chlorophyll by 47%.
steps: Graph A: survival falls from 100% to about 20% with water stress, so most plants die and yield is lost.

Closed pores (guard cells lose water and become flaccid) mean less carbon dioxide enters the leaf, and chlorophyll falls by 47% (less magnesium absorbed), so less light is absorbed, so photosynthesis and the supply of sugars for growth fall.
Graph B: cellulose content falls by about 21% (about 25% to about 20% dry mass), the error bars do not overlap, so the cell walls are weaker and less new cell wall can be made for growth.
Graph C: roots are about 55% shorter (about 8.9 cm to about 4 cm, small error bars), so there is less surface area to absorb water and ions, which makes water stress worse.

Own knowledge: water is also needed for turgor to expand cells, as a reactant in photosynthesis and to transport minerals in the xylem, so shortage reduces cell elongation and growth, and leads to wilting.

questions.question: Label the tonoplast on the incomplete plant cell diagram drawn by the student.
questions.answer: Label line to the membrane that surrounds the large central vacuole (the boundary of the grey T-shaped sac inside the cell wall), labelled tonoplast.
steps: The tonoplast is the single membrane that surrounds the permanent vacuole.
The large grey T-shaped sac in the middle of the cell is the vacuole, so draw a label line that ends on its outline (the thin boundary line of the grey sac) and write "tonoplast".
The line should not end in the middle of the vacuole (that is the cell sap) or on the thick outer cell wall.

questions.question: Draw and label a nucleolus in the plant cell on the student's diagram.
questions.answer: Draw a small dark circle inside the nucleus (the small oval at the top of the cell) and label it nucleolus.
steps: The nucleolus is a dense, round body inside the nucleus where ribosomal RNA is made.
The nucleus is the small oval near the top of the cell, so draw a small, darker filled circle inside the oval, well inside the nuclear envelope.
Label it "nucleolus" with a label line that ends on the circle.

questions.question: Complete the table to show which structures would be present or absent in plant leaf cells.
questions.answer: Amyloplast: x; chloroplast: tick; Golgi apparatus: tick; plasmodesmata: tick.
steps: Plant leaf cells contain chloroplasts, which carry out photosynthesis, so chloroplast is present.
Amyloplasts are the starch-storing plastids of non-photosynthetic storage tissue (roots, tubers, seeds), so they are absent from leaf cells (leaf starch is stored in the chloroplasts).
Golgi apparatus is present in all eukaryotic cells, and plasmodesmata link neighbouring plant cells through their walls, so both are present.

questions.question: Calculate the actual width (X-Y) of the lysosome in the electron micrograph, in micrometres, to two decimal places.
steps: Measure X-Y on the image: about 35 mm on the printed page (125 px at 745 px per 210 mm); a ruler should give 34 mm to 36 mm.
Actual size = image size / magnification = 35 mm / 250 000 = 1.4 x 10^-4 mm.
Convert to micrometres: 1.4 x 10^-4 mm x 1000 = 0.14 um.

questions.question: The pollen tube growth rate is given as 0.2 m s-1 (prefix garbled in text). How long would it take to grow 15 mm? A 75 seconds, B 125 minutes, C 1 250 minutes, D 7 500 seconds.
questions.answer: C: 1 250 minutes
steps: Convert 15 mm to micrometres: 15 mm = 15 000 um.
Time = distance / rate = 15 000 um / 0.2 um s^-1 = 75 000 s.
Convert to minutes: 75 000 / 60 = 1 250 minutes, so C.

questions.question: State how to calculate the actual length of one of the pollen tubes in the photograph.
questions.answer: Measure the length on the image and divide by the magnification (or use the scale bar to convert to actual length).
steps: Measure the length of the pollen tube in the photograph, in millimetres.
Use the magnification of the photograph: actual length = image length / magnification.
Convert units as needed to give the actual length.

questions.topic: DNA Quantity in Embryo and Endosperm
questions.question: Explain why an embryo cell and an endosperm cell contain different quantities of DNA, given that the embryo forms from the egg and the endosperm from the polar nuclei.
questions.answer: The embryo cell is diploid (2n) from a haploid egg and a haploid male nucleus; the endosperm cell is triploid (3n) from two haploid polar nuclei and a haploid male nucleus.
steps: The egg cell is haploid (n) and the male gamete nucleus is haploid (n).
Their fusion forms the zygote, which is diploid (2n), and develops into the embryo.
The two polar nuclei are haploid, and fuse with a second male nucleus.
This gives a triploid (3n) endosperm nucleus, so endosperm cells have more DNA than embryo cells.

questions.question: Describe a drug trial method to determine whether an extract from the Madonna lily is safe for humans and more effective than the current hospital skin burn treatment.
questions.answer: Test safety in a phase I trial with small doses, then compare effectiveness in a larger double-blind randomised trial against the current hospital treatment, measuring healing and side effects.
steps: Phase I: test the extract on a small group of healthy volunteers or patients to find a safe dose and side effects.
Phase II: give a range of doses to patients with skin burns to find an effective dose.
Phase III: randomly allocate a larger group of burn patients to the extract or the current hospital treatment.
Use a double-blind design so neither patients nor clinicians know which treatment is given.
Measure healing time and side effects in each group, and use statistics to compare effectiveness.

questions.question: Complete the table to show in which types of cells the listed structures are present or absent.
questions.answer: Amyloplast: animal x, plant tick, prokaryotic x; circular DNA: animal x, plant x, prokaryotic tick; mitochondria: animal tick, plant tick, prokaryotic x; nucleolus: animal tick, plant tick, prokaryotic x.
steps: Amyloplasts store starch and are found only in plant cells (they are plastids).
Circular DNA is the main chromosome of prokaryotes (plus plasmids); the nuclear DNA of animal and plant cells is linear (though the small DNA inside their mitochondria and chloroplasts is circular).
Mitochondria are present in animal and plant (eukaryotic) cells but prokaryotes have none, so tick, tick, x.
The nucleolus is inside the nucleus of eukaryotic cells, so it is present in animal and plant cells but absent from prokaryotes, which have no nucleus.

questions.question: The smallest living cell has diameter 0.2 m. Which option shows its volume in standard form? A 4.2 x 10^-3 m3, B 4.2 x 10^3 m3, C 3.4 x 10^-2 m3, D 3.4 x 10^2 m3.
steps: Radius = diameter / 2 = 0.1 m.
Volume of a sphere = 4/3 x pi x r^3 = 4/3 x 3.14 x (0.1)^3.
= 4.19 x 10^-3 m3, which is 4.2 x 10^-3 m3 in standard form, answer A.

questions.question: Which statements about human sperm cells are correct? 1 same quantity of DNA as a body cell, 2 contain hydrolytic enzymes, 3 release of energy from starch enables flagellum rotation. A 1, 2 and 3, B 2 and 3 only, C 2 only, D 3 only.
questions.answer: C 2 only
steps: Statement 1 is wrong: sperm are haploid, with half the DNA of a body cell.
Statement 2 is correct: the acrosome contains hydrolytic enzymes that digest the egg coat.
Statement 3 is wrong: sperm use glucose from respiration, not starch, to power the flagellum.
Only statement 2 is correct, so the answer is C.

questions.question: Evaluate the proposal to inject recently obtained sperm into egg cells with a zona pellucida thicker than 18 micrometres during IVF, using the table of zona pellucida thicknesses.
questions.answer: The proposal has some support: unfertilised eggs have a thicker zona pellucida (18.9 against 16.6 um), but the large standard deviations show a big overlap, so thickness alone is a weak guide and injection brings risks and costs.
steps: For: the mean zona pellucida thickness is greater in unfertilised eggs (18.9 +/- 4.0 um) than in fertilised eggs (16.6 +/- 3.2 um), so a thick zona pellucida (more than 18 um) may stop sperm penetrating it, and injecting sperm directly into the egg bypasses this barrier.

Against: the standard deviations are large and the ranges overlap (13.4 to 19.8 against 14.9 to 22.9 um), so the difference may not be significant and many fertilised eggs also have a zona above 18 um; the sample size is not given.

The sperm should be injected soon after collection because a longer time between ejaculation and reaching the egg may reduce fertilisation (sperm age, motility and viability fall), which supports using recently obtained sperm.
Disadvantages of injection: the egg can be damaged, it is invasive and expensive, it bypasses natural selection of the sperm (and may pass on male infertility), and ethical views vary.
Overall: it may help for eggs with a thick zona, but more data (success rates, larger samples, a significance test) are needed before using the 18 um cut-off.

questions.question: Estimate the height of the sunflower shown in the diagram, giving units.
steps: Scale from the person: the 1.6 m person is about 211 units tall on the diagram.
The sunflower is about 344 units tall (measure both arrows with a ruler).
Height = 344 / 211 x 1.6 m = 2.6 m (ruler measurements should give a ratio of about 1.6).

questions.question: Name the tissue that would contain structure X shown in the photograph of a structure in a sunflower plant.
questions.answer: Phloem
steps: Structure X is a plate with many large pores across the end wall of a tube, which is a sieve plate.
Sieve plates are found between sieve tube elements in the phloem, so the tissue is phloem.

questions.question: Describe how two structures in the tissue named in part (b)(i) enable it to carry out its function.
questions.answer: Sieve plates (pores let sucrose solution flow from one sieve tube element to the next) and companion cells (mitochondria supply ATP for loading sucrose).
steps: Structure 1, sieve plate: the pores in the end walls allow the phloem sap with dissolved sugars (assimilates) to pass from one sieve tube element to the next.

Structure 2, companion cell: connected to the sieve tube element by plasmodesmata, it has many mitochondria and makes ATP for active loading of sucrose into the sieve tube (it also supplies the proteins that the sieve tube needs).
Other acceptable structures: sieve tube elements have little cytoplasm, no nucleus and few organelles, which leaves space and lowers resistance to flow.

questions.question: Which tissues contain lignin? 1 phloem, 2 sclerenchyma, 3 xylem. A 1 only, B 1 and 3 only, C 2 and 3 only, D 3 only.
questions.answer: C 2 and 3 only
steps: Lignin is deposited in the walls of sclerenchyma fibres and xylem vessels.
Phloem sieve tubes do not contain lignin.
So statements 2 and 3 are correct: answer C.

questions.question: Suggest two reasons why a climbing plant growing up a bamboo pole may have a lower lignin content than a sunflower of the same height and diameter.
questions.answer: The climbing plant does not need to support its own weight as much because the pole supports it, so it invests less in lignin; it can put energy into growth and flexible stems instead.
steps: A climbing plant uses an existing structure (the bamboo pole) for support.
So it does not need as much lignified, rigid tissue as a free-standing sunflower of the same height.
Lignin is energetically expensive to make, so the climber saves resources for growth and leaf production.

questions.question: Describe how the structure and arrangement of cellulose microfibrils in xylem vessel walls contribute to their functions.
questions.answer: Cellulose chains are unbranched and hydrogen bonded into microfibrils that give tensile strength; microfibrils in layers and lignified rings or spirals stop the vessel collapsing while allowing water flow through the lumen.
steps: Cellulose molecules are long, unbranched chains of beta-glucose.
Chains are linked by hydrogen bonds into microfibrils, which have high tensile strength.
Microfibrils are laid down in rings or spirals in the secondary wall.
This arrangement resists the negative pressure of water tension, so the vessel does not collapse and water can flow through the open lumen.

questions.question: Give two conclusions for the effect of EDTA and citric acid on the calcium ion content in the roots of two types of maize, using the graph.
questions.answer: Both EDTA and citric acid reduce the calcium ion content of the roots in both types of maize; EDTA affects type A more, and citric acid affects type B more.
steps: Conclusion 1: with no treatment both types contain about 6.3 mg calcium per gram of dry mass, and both EDTA and citric acid lower the calcium content of the roots in both types.
Conclusion 2: EDTA lowers type A much more than type B (about 6.3 to 4.3, a 32% fall, against about 6.3 to 5.7, a 9% fall).
Citric acid has the larger effect on type B (about 6.3 to 4.4, a 31% fall) than on type A (about 6.3 to 5.3, a 16% fall), so the two types respond differently to the chemicals.

questions.question: Explain the effect that EDTA would have on new cell walls in the roots of type A maize plants.
questions.answer: EDTA binds (chelates) calcium ions, so less free calcium is available to cross-link pectin in the new cell walls, making them weaker.
steps: EDTA is a chelating agent that binds metal ions such as calcium strongly.
Calcium ions are needed to cross-link pectin chains in the middle lamella and new cell walls.
With calcium bound to EDTA, less calcium is free for cross-linking.
So new cell walls are weaker and less rigid.

questions.question: Describe how post-transcriptional changes convert pre-mRNA into active mRNA.
questions.answer: Introns are removed and exons joined by splicing; a 5' cap and poly-A tail are added, giving mature mRNA that is exported and translated.
steps: Pre-mRNA is a copy of both introns (non-coding) and exons (coding) from the gene.
Splicing removes the introns and joins the exons together to form continuous coding sequence.
A 5' cap is added to the start, and a poly-A tail to the end, to protect the mRNA and aid export.
The mature mRNA is then exported from the nucleus to the cytoplasm for translation.

questions.question: Structure Y (a ribosome) can be in the cytoplasm or on the surface of an organelle. Which organelle has structure Y on its surface? A Golgi apparatus, B mitochondria, C rough endoplasmic reticulum, D smooth endoplasmic reticulum.
questions.answer: C rough endoplasmic reticulum
steps: Structure Y is a ribosome, the site of translation.
Ribosomes attach to the outer surface of rough endoplasmic reticulum.
Smooth ER, Golgi and mitochondria do not have ribosomes on their surface.

questions.question: Give the function of structure Y, the ribosome.
questions.answer: Protein synthesis: it translates mRNA into a polypeptide chain.
steps: Ribosomes read the codons on mRNA.
Transfer RNA brings the matching amino acids.
Amino acids are joined by peptide bonds to form a polypeptide.

questions.question: Which row gives the names of the molecules labelled X and Z in the diagram of translation?
questions.answer: B: X is a polypeptide and Z is an RNA strand (mRNA)
steps: The diagram shows translation: a ribosome (large and small subunit) moves along an mRNA strand and makes a growing chain of amino acids.
Molecule X is the beaded chain growing out of the ribosome, which is a polypeptide (a chain of amino acids), not a polysaccharide.
Molecule Z is the strand passing between the two subunits that is being read by the ribosome, which is mRNA (an RNA strand), not DNA; so the row is polypeptide and RNA strand, B.

questions.question: Suggest the role of the enzyme DNA methyltransferase (DNMT) in DNA methylation.
questions.answer: DNMT adds methyl groups to cytosine bases (often in CpG sites) on DNA, which typically silences the gene by blocking transcription.
steps: DNA methyltransferase is an enzyme that transfers methyl groups from a donor molecule.
It adds methyl groups to cytosine bases in the DNA, often at CpG sites.
Methylation of the promoter region prevents transcription factors binding, so the gene is switched off.

questions.question: Explain how treatment with Peperomin E and the other drug affect the activity of the RASSF1 gene and the changes in tumour volume, using graph A and your own knowledge.
questions.answer: Methylation switches off the tumour suppressor gene RASSF1; peperomin E demethylates it so RASSF1 is expressed again and tumour growth is slowed (more at 50 mg kg^-1), but the current drug (group D) is the most effective.
steps: With no treatment (group A) the RASSF1 gene stays methylated, so it is silenced and its protein is not made; cells divide without control, and the relative tumour volume rises from 1 to about 4.9 and the mean tumour mass is about 455 mg at 21 days.
Peperomin E causes demethylation of the RASSF1 gene, so it can be transcribed and translated again; the RASSF1 protein slows cell division or causes cell death, so tumours grow more slowly.

At 25 mg kg^-1 (group B) the volume at 21 days is about 2.8 (43% less than A) and the mass about 285 mg (37% less); at 50 mg kg^-1 (group C) the volume is about 2.5 (49% less) and the mass about 200 mg (56% less), so a higher dose gives a greater effect (dose-dependent) though the extra effect is small.

The current drug (group D) is the most effective: the tumour volume rises only to about 1.8 by day 13 and then falls to about 1.55 (68% less than A), and the mass is about 170 mg (63% less than A); it may also reactivate genes or act in another way (the page does not describe its action).
All the treatments keep the tumour smaller than no treatment, but none removes it; peperomin E may have fewer side effects, and only 10 mice per group were used, so more tests are needed.

questions.question: Calculate the ratio of cellulose to lignin for a one-year-old bamboo plant, from the graph of mean percentages.
steps: Read the bars for 1 year: cellulose is about 55% and lignin is about 28%.
Ratio cellulose : lignin = 55 / 28 = 1.96.
So the ratio is about 2.0 : 1 (1.96 : 1).

questions.topic: Effect of Age on Bamboo Composition
questions.question: Give one conclusion about the effect of age on the mean percentage of cellulose and lignin in bamboo plants.
questions.answer: As the bamboo plant gets older, the percentage of cellulose decreases while the percentage of lignin increases.
steps: Cellulose falls from about 55% at 1 year to about 45% at 5 years.
Lignin rises from about 28% at 1 year to about 40% at 5 years, so the ratio of cellulose to lignin falls with age.

questions.question: Explain how the arrangement of molecules in the xylem cell walls contributes to the high tensile strength of bamboo.
questions.answer: Cellulose chains are arranged in microfibrils held by hydrogen bonds, giving tensile strength; lignin fills and cross-links the wall, adding rigidity and resistance to compression.
steps: Cellulose molecules form long chains that are hydrogen bonded into microfibrils.
Microfibrils resist stretching and give tensile strength along the length of the stem.
Lignin is deposited within and around the microfibrils, adding rigidity.
The combination of cellulose tensile strength and lignin rigidity makes the bamboo strong.

questions.question: Which are the structures labelled X in the photograph of part of a bamboo cell wall? A amyloplasts, B chloroplasts, C plasmodesmata, D tonoplasts.
questions.answer: C: plasmodesmata
steps: X points to small round holes (pits or pores) in the plant cell wall.
Channels through the cell wall that link neighbouring plant cells are plasmodesmata, so C.
Amyloplasts and chloroplasts are organelles inside cells and tonoplasts are the vacuole membranes, so none of these appears as holes in a wall.

questions.question: Which are functions of xylem vessels? 1 support, 2 translocation of organic solutes to the leaves, 3 transport of inorganic ions to the leaves, 4 transport of water to the leaves. A 1, 2 and 3 only, B 1, 3 and 4 only, C 1 and 3 only, D 1 and 4 only.
questions.answer: B 1, 3 and 4 only
steps: Statement 1 is correct: xylem vessels with lignified walls provide support.
Statement 2 is wrong: translocation of organic solutes is done by phloem.
Statement 3 is correct: xylem carries inorganic ions upwards.
Statement 4 is correct: xylem carries water to the leaves, so answer B.

questions.topic: Phloem and Xylem Distribution in Leaf
questions.question: Give one difference between the distribution of phloem and xylem in a leaf compared with their distribution in a transverse section of a stem.
questions.answer: In the leaf the xylem is above (towards the upper surface) and the phloem below (towards the lower surface) in each vein; in the stem the xylem is inside and the phloem outside the bundle.
steps: In a leaf vein the xylem is on the upper (adaxial) side and the phloem on the lower (abaxial) side of the vein, as the diagram shows.
In a stem vascular bundle the xylem is on the inner side (towards the centre) and the phloem on the outer side (towards the epidermis).
Also, the leaf bundles are spread along the flat blade in one row, whereas the stem bundles form a ring near the outside of the stem.

questions.question: Explain why a drinking cup made from sugarcane parts left over from sugar production is a sustainable product.
questions.answer: It uses a by-product (waste) of sugar production, which is renewable, so it does not use an extra finite resource, and it biodegrades.
steps: The cup is made from parts of the sugarcane left over from sugar production, so it uses a waste product.
Sugarcane is a renewable crop that can be grown again each year.
Using a by-product avoids consuming new finite resources.
The plant material biodegrades, so it does not persist as pollution.

questions.question: Comment on the results of the investigation of olive oil extract antimicrobial properties at low and high concentrations, using the graph of living bacteria over time.
questions.answer: The extract kills bacteria: the number of living bacteria falls with time, faster with the high concentration (none left after 5 hours) than the low concentration (none after 7 hours), whereas the control stays at about 7.6 x 10^6 per cm^3.
steps: Control: the number of living bacteria stays at about 7.6 to 7.9 x 10^6 per cm^3 for 7 h, so the fall in the other tubes is due to the extract.
Low concentration: the number falls from 7.6 to 6.1 (0.5 h), 4.9 (1 h), 3.3 (3 h) and 1.9 (5 h), and none at 7 h.

High concentration: the number falls more quickly, to 4.1 (0.5 h), 3.3 (1 h) and 2.2 (3 h), and there are no living bacteria at 5 h or 7 h, so a higher concentration is more effective (43% fewer than the control at 1 h for low and 57% for high).

The error bars are small and do not overlap between treatments at the same time, so the differences are probably significant; the extract has an antimicrobial (bactericidal) effect that depends on the time and the concentration.

questions.question: State the relationship between the time spent in interphase and the number of white blood cells, using the graph.
questions.answer: As the time in interphase decreases, the number of cells increases (a negative relationship).
steps: Time in interphase falls from about 180 hours (0 PHA) to about 5 hours at 1.0 ug cm^-3.
Over the same range the number of cells rises from about 2 to 16 x 10^6 per cm^3, so the shorter the interphase the more cells there are.

questions.question: Which is the correct percentage change in cell number from 0.0 to 1.0 g cm-3 of PHA? A -700%, B -87.5%, C +87.5%, D +700%.
steps: Number of cells at 0.0 ug cm^-3 is 2 x 10^6 per cm^3 and at 1.0 ug cm^-3 it is 16 x 10^6 per cm^3.
Change = 16 - 2 = 14, so percentage change = 14 / 2 x 100 = +700%.

questions.question: Explain the results of the investigation into the effect of PHA on white blood cell number and time in interphase.
questions.answer: PHA shortens interphase, so the cell cycle is faster and more cell divisions take place, giving more cells.
steps: As the concentration of PHA rises, the time spent in interphase falls steeply from about 180 hours to about 5 hours, so the cell cycle is much shorter.

A shorter cell cycle means that the cells complete DNA replication and cell growth sooner, so they enter mitosis and divide more often in the same time, so the number of cells increases (from 2 to 16 x 10^6 per cm^3, 8 times as many).

Above about 0.4 to 0.6 ug cm^-3 the time in interphase hardly falls and the number of cells rises more slowly, because interphase cannot be shortened below a minimum (mitosis and cytokinesis still take time).
PHA is therefore acting as a mitogen, stimulating the cells to divide.

questions.question: Give two reasons why water is important to strawberry plants.
questions.answer: Water is a solvent for ions and substances transported in the xylem, and it is a raw material for photosynthesis (and provides turgor).
steps: Water is a solvent, so it dissolves inorganic ions and carries them through the xylem.
Water is a reactant in photosynthesis, providing hydrogen for making glucose.
Water maintains turgor pressure in cells, keeping leaves and stems firm.

questions.question: Explain the importance of nitrate ions and calcium ions to strawberry plants.
questions.answer: Nitrate supplies nitrogen for amino acids, proteins and nucleotides; calcium cross-links pectin in cell walls and middle lamella and helps maintain membrane structure and signalling.
steps: Nitrate is a source of nitrogen for making amino acids and proteins.
Nitrogen is also needed for nucleotides, DNA and RNA.
Calcium ions cross-link pectin chains in the middle lamella, strengthening cell walls.
Calcium also helps keep cell membranes stable and acts as a cell signal.

questions.question: Continent Q produced 634 288 000 kg of strawberries in 2021. Which is the mass produced in continent S? A 61 136 193 kg, B 760 212 883 kg, C 2 183 071 550 kg, D 4 531 720 288 kg.
steps: The mass of strawberries is proportional to the angle of the sector.
Continent Q has 24.9 degrees for 634 288 000 kg, so continent S (85.7 degrees) = 634 288 000 x 85.7 / 24.9.
= 2 183 071 550 kg, which is C.

questions.topic: Percentage Difference in Wheat Grain Mass
questions.question: Calculate the percentage difference in mean mass of wheat grains per square metre between groups A and B, using the table.
questions.answer: -11% (A is 11.4% lower than B)
steps: Percentage difference = (A - B) / ((A + B) / 2) x 100, with A = 0.58 and B = 0.65 kg m^-2.
Percentage difference = -0.07 / 0.615 x 100 = -11.4%, so group A has a mean grain mass 11.4% lower than group B (about -11%).

questions.question: Discuss the farmers' conclusion that they would make more money by adding magnesium ions to wheat, using the table of grain mass and gluten content and your own knowledge.
questions.answer: The conclusion is supported: magnesium increased both grain mass and gluten content, so the farmers would get more and higher-value flour, as long as the cost of the magnesium is less than the extra income.
steps: Group A (no magnesium) had the lowest values: 0.58 kg m^-2 of grain and 265 g gluten per kg.

Magnesium on the leaves (group B) raised grain mass by 12% to 0.65 and gluten by 7% to 283; magnesium in the nutrient solution (group C) raised grain by 16% to 0.67 and gluten by 12% to 298; the total gluten per m^2 rose from about 154 g to 184 g (B) and 200 g (C).
More gluten means a higher protein content, and flour with a higher protein content is more expensive, so the farmers would earn more per kg as well as having a greater mass.
Magnesium is part of chlorophyll (more photosynthesis, more growth and grain) and activates enzymes for protein synthesis, so the results are biologically sensible.

Evaluation: group C is only slightly better than B for the grain (0.67 against 0.65), so spraying leaves may be a cheaper way of adding magnesium; but there is no cost information, no standard deviations or repeats, only one wheat variety and hydroponic conditions, so the profit cannot be proved.
